articles.title: Ex-Purdue star Trey Kaufman-Renn granted TRO to return to college basketball in latest eligibility ruling
articles.summary: Trey Kaufman-Renn was selected in the second round of the NBA Draft earlier this summer by the Timberwolves, but he never signed a contract with them.
articles.body:
Trey Kaufman-Renn may be able to play a sixth season of college basketball after all.

The former Purdue star was granted a temporary restraining order against the NCAA by a circuit court in Indiana's Clark County on Wednesday, according to the Indianapolis Star . He is just the latest player throughout college sports to receive a similar order in recent weeks and months.

Kaufman-Renn will have a hearing for a preliminary injunction in the future, which would serve as a long-term solution. He will likely need that in order to actually play college basketball this season, at Purdue or elsewhere. That hearing has not been scheduled. His move to return to college came after the NCAA's new five-in-five rule, which was announced in June — something Kaufman-Renn wasn't able to benefit from.

Kaufman-Renn played four seasons for Purdue after initially redshirting, and earned all-Big Ten honors during his junior campaign. He averaged 14.2 points and 8.3 rebounds last season with the Boilermakers, who he helped lead to the Elite Eight. Kaufman-Renn was a key piece on their team that reached the national championship game in 2024, too.

Kaufman-Renn then entered the NBA Draft this past summer, and he was selected in the second round by the Minnesota Timberwolves. He played for them in the NBA Summer League in Las Vegas. But Kaufman-Renn has not signed a professional contract with the Timberwolves yet, and likely wasn't on track to earn a spot in their active roster.

Even if Kaufman-Renn is granted his preliminary injunction, it's unclear where he would actually end up. All four power conferences have passed similar rulings recently banning players who participated in pro football from returning to the college level. Some of those leagues have included basketball in their initial policies, while others are expected to announce that in the future.

LSU has been at the center of the debate after attempting to add two players who signed NFL contracts, though the Tigers have since backed down. SEC schools are still expected to meet and discuss LSU and its future membership in the league.

Several players who either played in the G League or entered the NBA Draft attempted to return last year. Alabama's Charles Bediako was perhaps the most notable, but he only appeared in five games before his TRO was overruled . Baylor signed former NBA Draft pick James Nnaji in December, too, but he never played in an NBA game and instead was with FC Barcelona since 2020. Two other former G League players are set to play for programs next season, too.

It's unclear where Kaufman-Renn plays this season, or if he ends up getting to at all. But the first step on that quest has gone in his favor.

articles.title: Deni Avdija Projected To Leave Trail Blazers And Become Premium NBA Free Agent
articles.summary: Portland Trail Blazers called "sinking ship" as questions loom about Deni Avdija's future.
articles.body:
In today's NBA, teams have to be more careful than ever about who they spend their money on . With strict CBA rules and restrictions for teams that spend too much, many veteran players are caught in the middle as their own teams review their worth.

In Portland, this is the situation regarding Deni Avdija , who is coming off his first All-Star season with averages of 24.2 points, 6.9 rebounds, 6.7 assists, 0.8 steals, and 0.6 blocks per game on 46.2% shooting from the field. As much as he has thrived with the Trail Blazers , they are not in a position to extend his contract after the conclusion of his current deal, which only has two years and $24 million left.

"The Blazers are kind of a sinking ship. They are not setting themselves up to preserve the cap space they're gonna need to renegotiate and extend Deni Avdija ," said insider Sam Quinn on the 'Third Apron' podcast . "Deni will make $11.875 million in 2027-28. The most he can get in a veteran extension is a 140% Year 1 raise, or $16.625 million. That's MLE money. He's not taking that. To pay him fairly, they'd need cap space to renegotiate and extend him."

The Trail Blazers have made strides of late, thanks to the heroic performances of Avdija, Scoot Henderson , Donovan Clingan , and young sharpshooter Shaedon Sharpe . On paper, they have a solid young core that will only get better on the floor, but critics remain doubtful of their current trajectory.

Besides the injury to Sharpe ( that will keep him out for months ), the Trail Blazers must also deal with the reality of their frugal owner, Tom Dundon, who has already made headlines for his cost-cutting methods . That's not to mention the logjam in the backcourt between guards Ja Morant , Damian Lillard , Jrue Holiday , and Scoot Henderson . By all accounts, the Trail Blazers are a team with glaring red flags, and Avdija clearly does not fit their timeline as a win-now veteran in his prime.

Rather than pay Deni to stick around and handicap their flexibility, the Trail Blazers are expected to let him go as they make space for their younger generation. Whether he leaves via trade or free agency in 2028, he will likely have to look elsewhere to secure the max-level deal he'll no doubt be seeking. The question is, where would the best fit be?

It's hard to predict what the situation will look like, but Avdija is the kind of player who can raise any team's ceiling. That's why we can expect multiple teams to express interest in a contract, including potentially the Clippers , Suns , and Rockets , who all have the incentive to strike a deal. There's also the Denver Nuggets , where Avdija could make a fitting replacement for Peyton Watson (at the right price).

For now, with two years left on his contract, the Trail Blazers are going to stick with who they have and see where they stand. Eventually, however, they will need to make a choice, and it could very well shake up the NBA hierarchy in a major way.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark Reveals Coach K's Advice to WNBA Star Ahead Team USA's 2026 FIBA World Cup Run
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark and the United States women's team will take the court Thursday for the quarterfinals of the 2026 FIBA World Cup, and she studied the advice of a legendary coach to better prepare her for the moment.
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark and the United States women's team will take the court Thursday for the quarterfinals of the 2026 FIBA World Cup, and she studied the advice of a legendary coach to better prepare her for the moment.

Doug Feinberg of the Associated Press reported Wednesday that Clark watched videos of former Team USA and Duke men's coach Mike Krzyzewski talking about assimilating to a star-studded national team roster with players such as LeBron James and Kobe Bryant.

The message that the only thing that matters is winning on this stage is what resonated with the Indiana Fever star.

"You have to set everything that you want to achieve personally aside," Clark said. "At the end of the day, people don't care about that if you have a gold medal hanging around your neck. So, that's my goal, and I think we have the group to do it."

The United States has won the last four editions of this tournament and last fell short in 2006 when it settled for the bronze. This year is once again gold-medal-or-bust with so many WNBA superstars leading the way, and that can be a motivating factor.

"You don't want to be the team that everybody talks about because you didn't win," Clark said. "You want to do what's expected and that's to win a gold medal. I think it would certainly help and hopefully it's just a step in the direction of where I want to keep building and hopefully the goals that I want to achieve of hopefully playing in the Olympics in '28."

The Americans have looked the part of gold-medal favorite thus far with a 3-0 record in group play, although they received quite a test from Italy.

While Clark and Co. handled China by 33 points and Czechia by 41 points, they trailed Italy in the fourth quarter before escaping with a 55-52 victory. Perhaps it was something of a wake-up call and an experience they can build on moving into the elimination rounds.

As for Clark, she wasted no time establishing herself with a double-double of 14 points and 11 assists in the opener against China. However, she had just one point and one assist against Italy before going 1-of-6 from deep on the way to nine points against Czechia.

Fortunately for her, she doesn't have to be the star every night on a team that includes Napheesa Collier, Breanna Stewart, Paige Bueckers, Angel Reese, Jackie Young and more.

"Obviously there's probably still a lot of pressure on me to perform at this level, but I think that's a great thing about USA basketball, it isn't like the WNBA," the Fever guard said. "You're probably not going to come out here and score 30 and have 10 assists. That's just not reality because of the talent we have."

That is exactly the message Coach K preached in the videos she watched.

articles.title: LSU President Wade Rousse ends Lane Kiffin’s SEC showdown, but there is still relationships to mend
articles.summary: A Birmingham Alabama federal court hearing was delayed after LSU backed down and finalized its roster without former pro-athletes Wright or Harris.
articles.body: The ongoing battle between the SEC and LSU was set to be heard in a courtroom on Wednesday afternoon in Birmingham, Alabama. But, just 10 minutes before the scheduled hearing in federal court over whether the SEC would be granted the power to enforce its rules pertaining to former pro-athletes returning to college athletics, lawyers for both sides met inside the chambers of the presiding judge to discuss a resolution. A decision was made to continue the case to a later date, if needed and cooler heads looked to prevail out of Baton Rouge. LSU HOLDS OFF ON ADDING PLAYERS WITH NFL TIES AS SEC LAWSUIT LOOMS OVER PROGRAM, LANE KIFFIN Call it 'waving the white flag' or however you'd prefer, but LSU has backed down from its stance on adding players to their roster that have professional experience in some form or fashion. One night before the SEC was scheduled to ask a federal judge in Alabama for a temporary restraining order, LSU has finalized its roster for the upcoming season. That doesn’t mean the SEC is not going to be meeting on Thursday regarding potential punishments for the LSU Tigers, though. JUDGE GRANTS INJUNCTION AGAINST NCAA, SEC, ALLOWING ATHLETES WITH NFL TIES ELIGIBLE TO PLAY FOR LSU, OTHERS After nearly three weeks of court appearances involving multiple athletes in the Louisiana case, including former Ole Miss players Dae’Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris, the Tigers decided not to add either player to its roster at any point this season. The decision comes after both sides were embroiled in a fight that saw SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey make an appearance in a Louisiana district court to testify on behalf of his conference. During those proceedings, the lawsuit filed by the SEC was brought up during questioning. INSIDE A LOUISIANA COURTROOM: SEC-LSU LEGAL CIRCUS PLAYED OUT LIKE A JOHN GRISHAM NOVEL IN STUNNING SHOWDOWN "Did you authorize the SEC to sue LSU and coach Lane Kiffin?" attorney Tony Clayton asked Sankey. When asked why the conference took that step, Sankey pointed to the authority of the presidents and chancellors he represents. "We established our First Amendment right for freedom of association, so that our conference can make decisions and our members can make decisions about membership," Sankey said. At that point, all options were on the table of how to move forward. Judging by the decision of LSU on Tuesday night into Wednesday morning, it was starting to become much clearer that the Tigers had finally backed down. LSU sends letter to SEC about complying with the rules The back-and-forth between all parties involved came to a head last Friday, when SEC presidents and chancellors had seen enough. At one point, a number of school officials were prepared to punish the school, with the topic of expulsion being brought up numerous times. While this never felt like a realistic option, the threat weighed heavy on the minds of folks around Baton Rouge. In a letter sent to SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey on Wednesday morning, and obtained by OutKick, LSU President Wade Rousse wanted to make it clear that the Tigers were going to comply with conference rules and not roster any of the athletes who would have been eligible under a court injunction. "On the afternoon of September 4, 2026, I called and provided you with advance notice that LSU would not place Dae'Quan Wright or Zxavian Harris on the football roster," President Rousse explained. "This was confirmed when LSU submitted its roster later that evening. On September 8, 2026, LSU filled its two remaining roster spots with eligible student-athletes. The roster is now locked for the season. "LSU complied with SEC rules. The issue is now mute." In terms of the meeting that was scheduled for Thursday between SEC presidents and chancellors to vote on what type of punishments to levy against LSU for this whole saga, President Rousse tried to make it clear that there would not be a challenge from the school, but the issue was now finalized. "Also on September 8, 2026, I received notice of the special President's and Chancellor's meeting scheduled for tomorrow, September 10, 2026. At no point has LSU ever threatened to upset that meeting," President Rousse explained. "But to be clear, LSU will not challenge, disrupt or seek to cancel or postpone this meeting. "This issue is also moot." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! LSU backed down, finally realized it wasn’t worth the fight All of this could have transpired weeks ago, when the SEC released its guidelines pertaining to rules on professional athletes returning to college sports. But, it looked as though the Tigers wanted to challenge the conference on its stance. While LSU was never actually named in the lawsuit pertaining to the athletes in a Baton Rouge court, they were certainly in the news. Thanks to statements from Governor Jeff Landry, along with Attorney General Liz Murrill showing up to the courthouse wearing a purple blouse and exclaiming 'Go Tigers' before entering the courthouse, it was obvious that while LSU officials were not present, government officials were trying to speak on their behalf. In reality, that's where this whole ordeal turned into a political sideshow that felt more like propaganda than the actual athletes involved in the case. Now, six days after the hearing inside a Baton Rouge court, the LSU Tigers are finally doing us all a favor and moving on from this nonsense that has diverted attention away from the college football season. And no, this does not mean we are done hearing about athletes from LSU being involved in legal arguments, as the school still has to make a decision on basketball player RJ Luis. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP We will see what the SEC decides to do on Thursday, but I think it's pretty clear that it was time for this circus to come to an end.

articles.title: Suns' Dillon Brooks Trains With UFC Fighter Li Jingliang in Video, Photos While in China
articles.summary: Phoenix Suns guard Dillon Brooks is undertaking a unique training regimen this offseason, working out with UFC fighter Li Jingliang in China.
articles.body:
Phoenix Suns guard Dillon Brooks is undertaking a unique training regimen this offseason, working out with UFC fighter Li Jingliang in China.

Brooks, 30, had his best season in 2025-26, averaging a career-high 20.2 points while adding 3.6 rebounds, 1.8 assists and one steal in 56 games. The Suns also surprisingly reached the postseason, though they were swept in four games against the Oklahoma City Thunder.

And now he's gearing up for a reprisal of that strong campaign by getting in some work with Jingliang.

articles.title: Stephen A Smith blasts SEC for threats to kick LSU out of the conference: 'Sit your a-- down'
articles.summary: Lane Kiffin's bold move to bring NFL-cut players back to LSU through the transfer portal sparked SEC threats to expel the Tigers from the conference.
articles.body: The 2026 college football season is off to a surprisingly controversial start. Out of nowhere, the Western Michigan-Michigan game became one of the most contentious finishes in recent memory, with replay review adding an additional second to the fourth quarter after the game had seemingly ended. That sparked a formal appeal from the MAC to the FBS Oversight Committee and the College Football Playoff to recognize the Broncos as the official winners, due to improper replay review procedures. Then there’s the human element: new LSU head coach Lane Kiffin. Kiffin drew criticism for his lengthy, drawn-out decision-making process after LSU offered him the job in Baton Rouge. His eventual decision to leave Ole Miss before the College Football Playoff made him public enemy No. 1 in Oxford. Somehow, the questions surrounding Kiffin have only deepened over time. LSU’S LANE KIFFIN FIRES BACK AT NFL RETURNEE BACKLASH: BLAME THE NCAA, NOT US FOR RECRUITING PRO ATHLETES Kiffin set about reshaping the Tigers' program through the transfer portal, then apparently had an even more unique and extreme idea: bring players who had signed with NFL teams but failed to make the regular season roster back to college football. Obviously designed to give LSU an advantage by adding more physically advanced and developed players, that tactic was immediately disparaged by opposing coaches, NFL coaches and, more importantly, the SEC itself. A war of words and policies ensued with multiple conferences, including the SEC, immediately passing a policy to prevent "pro" players returning to the collegiate ranks. LSU fought back, even winning an injunction to allow two players, Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris, to confirm their eligibility. That led to some extreme measures being discussed, including reports this week that the SEC was prepared to vote imminently to expel LSU from the conference entirely. As shocking and extreme as that sounds, it's clear that the SEC wanted to ensure that their commitment to "amateur" athletics remained unblemished. CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM Some supported the potential vote as a punishment for Kiffin and the Tigers program pushing the limits of eligibility. And further SEC filings implied that the athletic director had little control of the football team, with Kiffin alone running the ship. But Stephen A. Smith, apparently, strongly disagrees, saying that just signing a contract in the NFL does not make you an "NFL player." "Just because you enter a draft — if you haven’t signed a contract with the NFL team, you are not an NFL player," he said during a recent episode of "First Take" on ESPN. "If you haven’t been on a practice field, if you haven’t competed against NFL players, you are not an NFL player. You should be able to go back to college. That’s the one thing that I do feel." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Smith wasn't done there, saying that LSU being pushed into independence may actually help the program. "And oh, by the way, Notre Dame, and we got love for Notre Dame, they’re an independent," he added. "LSU, you wanna throw them out the SEC? Go ahead and do it. Watch, they ain’t gonna lose. They’ll be just fine…Could you imagine Lane Kiffin as an independent? Out there in the open market for the LSU brand? Please, they’ll get paid…The SEC, sit your a-- down! Sit your a-- down!" The Tigers seemingly backed down from their plan this week, signaling by adding two other players to their roster that they wouldn't bring in those former "NFL" players. But Smith seems to have a different perspective on this than most fans or rival administrators and coaches. Once you leave college and sign with an NFL team, that's it. You're done. That's how it's always been, and changing it now opens up a can of worms. Would a player who’s, say, only made the practice squad be considered an "NFL player" in Smith’s view? Or would they still be eligible to return? What about another who is on an active roster, but never enters a game? Or someone who plays just one game before getting hurt? Defining who and who isn't a professional becomes a game of Whac-A-Mole that shouldn't be necessary. articles.title: Así serán los cuartos: España jugará en último lugar
articles.standfirst: Las eliminatorias de cuartos, las puertas para las medallas, se jugarán íntegras este jueves
articles.summary: Las eliminatorias de cuartos, las puertas para las medallas, se jugarán íntegras este jueves
articles.body: El Italia - Australia, que cerró la serie de partidos de clasificación, compuso definitivamente el cuadro de cuartos de final del Mundial, es decir, la antesala de la lucha por las medallas. Ganar el partido de cuartos implica seguir en el torneo todo el fin de semana. Perder, es sellar el billete a casa, para alguna incluso antes de lo previsto. Este jueves, el Uber Arena albergará todos los partidos de cuartos en sesión continua. Después de que la FIBA dividiera los partidos de clasificación en dos por día (martes y miércoles) obligando por ejemplo a que China y Australia no tengan ni 24 horas de descanso o a que España tuviera que esperar hasta las 22.30 para conocer a su rival, los partidos de cuartos dejarán resueltas las semifinales este jueves. Y el apasionante programa que nos espera es el siguiente: Estados Unidos - Hungría (11.30) El partido más madrugador, extrañamente de Estados Unidos, cuando los aficionados en ese país están aún durmiendo (las 05.30 hora de la Costa Este). Será el partido del turno de la mañana, con las favoritas al oro, las norteamericanas, ante la resistencia, veremos por cuánto tiempo, de las húngaras. EEUU no ha hecho un torneo redondo. Ganó con claridad a China y aplastó a la República Checa, pero estuvo a punto de perder por primera vez en 20 años en el Mundial. Lo pasó muy mal ante Italia e incluso hubo polémica en la derrota transalpina. Hungría, dos victorias y una clara derrota ante Francia, no parece un equipo hecho para derrotar a las estadounidenses, sobre todo pensando que el vigente campeón irá ajustando cada vez más su juego con la llegada de las eliminatorias directas. Tras una de las grandes favoritas al oro, la otra. Francia mide su descomunal potencial ante China que logró colarse en los cuartos merced a un ajustadísimo triunfo ante Puerto Rico. La gigante Ziyu Zhang (2,23), pondrá a prueba el potentísimo juego interior francés. El galo es probablemente el equipo que mejor ha llegado a esta cita. Eso, unido al talento de jugadoras como Gaby Williams, Marine Johannes o Dominique Malonga hace al equipo europeo muy favorito en este duelo. Entramos en un territorio más igualado, los dos partidos de cuartos con el pronóstico más incierto. Bueno, relativamente, porque Bélgica, actual campeona de Europa y un quinteto titular fabuloso, debería poner fin a la aventura de la anfitriona. La selección de Miguel Méndez se mide a un coco en estos cuartos. España hizo los deberes de quedar líder de su grupo pero con eso afronta el camino con más espinas de todos: Australia, EEUU y, si hay milagro norteamericano, Francia en la final (hipotéticamente). A pesar de las bajas de las australianas, Alanna Smith y Ezi Magbegor, el oceánico es un equipo muy potente y que arrancó este Mundial con el objetivo de una medalla. Según el ránking FIBA, Australia es la tercera del mundo, por detrás de EEUU y Francia, y por delante de España (sexta). Además las australianas han ganado los cuatro partidos que han jugado ante España en los Mundiales (4-0). Aún así, no sería una sorpresa un triunfo de España que se ha ganado por méritos propios estar en las quinielas de los equipos que llegarán a las semifinales. Será el partido que cierre los cuartos de la Copa del Mundo.

articles.title: María Conde: "El de cuartos es el partido que te marca en un campeonato"
articles.standfirst: La jugadora de la selección atiende a MARCA poco antes de medirse a Australia en el Mundial
articles.summary: La jugadora de la selección atiende a MARCA poco antes de medirse a Australia en el Mundial
articles.body: María Conde (Madrid, 1997), es una de las jóvenes veteranas de una selección que quiere buscar algo grande en el Mundial femenino. Su concurso es capital en el esquema de una España que esta noche (20.45) buscará las semifinales y con ello la lucha por las medallas ante la potente Australia. Pregunta. Lo primero, ¿cómo está? Acabó el partido ante Japón con algunas molestias físicas. Respuesta. Estoy bien. Esto es un campeonato y son partidos duros y tenemos que ir solucionando lo que va apareciendo, pero estoy bien, con ganas y contenta de que hayamos podido descansar y a esperar para empezar a jugar. P. Tras la derrota ante Mali, España vivió un primer momento crítico. ¿Cómo lo vivió el vestuario? R. Juntándonos un poco de nuevo, al final hay que confiar en el trabajo que se hace en el día a día. El baloncesto, como muchísimos otros deportes, tienes días buenos, malos y regulares. Ese día seguramente se juntaron muchas cosas que salieron muy mal y, de haber salido otras un poquito menos mal, a lo mejor el resultado habría sido distinto. Entonces era un poco juntarnos de nuevo y decir, bueno, vamos a confiar en el trabajo que estamos haciendo y enfocarnos en el partido siguiente, que es realmente lo único importante. P. También hubo un momento peligroso ante Japón al final del primer tiempo. ¿Se pensó ahí que Alemania resolvía su partido y había que ganar a toda costa? R. No, ni lo miramos ni preguntamos porque daba igual. Al final, no daba igual, evidentemente, si hubiéramos perdido, pero creo que el objetivo de todo el mundo era ganar el partido sí o sí. Por lo tanto, lo que estuviera pasando en el otro pabellón no importaba. P. Usted es una joven veterana, con kilómetros en la selección pero con mucho recorrido aún. ¿Cómo ha mezclado en su opinión la nueva generación de jugadoras? R. Creo que se ha hecho un buen trabajo intentando juntar la frescura que traen las jugadoras jóvenes, el nuevo estilo de baloncesto hacia el que yo creo que está evolucionando el deporte en sí, y eso es algo a lo que ellas se han adaptado muy bien y a lo que las jugadoras con un poco más de experiencia, a lo mejor, pues hemos tenido que ir sumando pequeñas cosas y luego, desde nuestra parte, pues intentar traer un poco la tranquilidad, a lo mejor, o la calma de haber jugado más partidos en alta competición simplemente porque tenemos más años. Y, por lo tanto, poner un poco esas cosas. Luego ya está en el cuerpo técnico el ser capaces de leer en cada partido las cosas que están funcionando y por dónde tenemos que tirar. P. ¿Se ha producido ya el cambio generacional de esta selección? R. Supongo que depende desde donde mires el inicio de ese cambio. Si contamos esos últimos años de la plata de Río, de los oros de los siguientes europeos, creo que solo queda Alba en el equipo de esos años. Entonces, seguramente se habrá producido un cambio. ¿Qué tipo de éxitos o derrotas o victorias van a venir a partir de ahí? No lo sabemos. Las generaciones que están ahora, las jugadoras que ya forman parte de la selección, vienen con mucha fuerza, jugadoras con mucha calidad y muy bien entrenadas y seguramente vengan también generaciones fuertes por debajo. Vemos los resultados que está habiendo en categorías inferiores y, por lo tanto, pues creo que cabe ser tener cierta esperanza con que se está haciendo buen baloncesto pero al final, igual que crecemos nosotros, van creciendo el resto de selecciones. Vemos a Francia, a Bélgica incluso, compitiendo también en categorías inferiores, incluso a Eslovenia, selecciones que a lo mejor no han sido tan fuertes estos últimos años a nivel senior, pero que están haciendo las cosas muy bien en categorías inferiores y eso también es un poco una marca de que otros países se están poniendo las pilas en ese sentido y, por lo tanto, lo que podamos hacer va a depender también de nosotras y de seguir viniendo aquí, seguir viniendo con ganas de trabajar y seguir encontrando por qué camino tenemos que ir. P. ¿Se han marcado un listón en este campeonato de lo que sería un gran torneo o un exitazo? R. Yo creo que un exitazo sería ganar, evidentemente, porque eso es algo con lo que soñamos todas, jugadoras, entrenadores y cuerpo técnico que estamos aquí, no sólo de nuestra selección, sino de todas las selecciones, creo que todos venimos aquí a ganar, por lo tanto ese sería el gran éxito. Pero para mí un campeonato exitoso, del que estar orgullosos, es un poco el seguir haciendo las cosas de la manera en la que las queremos hacer, el estar felices con el trabajo hecho y por lo tanto si eso es, hacer un partido muy serio en cuartos y no llevarse la victoria, pues a lo mejor eso también es un buen resultado o a lo mejor es llegar a la final habiendo pasado por encima de Estados Unidos. Es que es muy difícil poner en papel qué es lo que queremos conseguir, evidentemente a todas nos encantaría conseguir una medalla, pero hay que ser muy conscientes del campeonato que estamos jugando y de los rivales que tenemos enfrente y por lo tanto el próximo partido, el de cuartos, pues seguramente sea el partido del campeonato y a partir de ahí, pues ya sabes que puedes entrar a la lucha de medallas o que estás fuera. P. No me diga que no ha fantaseado con la posibilidad de ganar el oro... R. No te sabría decir, porque yo creo que, como te digo, ilusión tenemos todas por llegar a ello porque es un mundial y todos los equipos y todas las jugadoras vienen aquí a ganar. Este año es muy diferente para todo el mundo porque se están dando cosas que no se han dado nunca. No ha habido ningún año nunca en la historia, creo, de este deporte en el que cada selección haya llegado con cinco, seis, siete, ocho jugadoras que no estaban en las concentraciones. Entonces podemos tener mucha ilusión y pensar que el equipo puede llegar muy lejos y de repente venir las cinco que hemos venido hace unos días y destrozar la dinámica o que las cosas que no salgan bien o que hayan construido estas jugadoras y, jugadoras que no están aquí y que podrían estar perfectamente en el equipo y que se merecían estar en el equipo. Ellas han estado construyendo cosas durante un mes y a lo mejor llegamos nosotras y no somos capaces de encajar en ello. Una cosa es en el papel decir que tenemos ilusión porque hay talento, hay trabajo y hay mucha gente que viene con muchas ganas y otra que se está dando algo que no se ha dado nunca y por lo tanto igual que nosotras pasa con China, con Francia, con Estados Unidos siempre, con Australia, con Bélgica, con todas las selecciones que vienen con mucha gente que se suma muy tarde y por lo tanto creo que es el campeonato en el que es más difícil pronosticar. Cada partido que pase será más fácil ver a los equipos, pero creo que es difícil decir por dónde van los tiros quién va a ser el equipo que va a ser capaz de ponerlo todo junto. P. Hoy tienen que medirse a Australia. ¿Cómo ve ese partido? R. Por lo que he visto Alanna Smith no jugará el resto del campeonato y eso es una baja importante para ellas pero siguen teniendo jugadoras con mucha experiencia tanto en la WNBA como internacional que para mí creo que es muy importante en este tipo de campeonatos FIBA porque los niveles de contacto también son distintos y Australia tiene muchas de estas jugadoras. Tiene una entrenadora con mucha experiencia, practican un juego que en cierta medida podría ser parecido al nuestro en los momentos en los que quieren jugar con transiciones muy rápidas jugar mucho en los primeros ocho segundos atacar mucho uno contra uno así que que creo que va a ser un partido en el que tenemos que empezar desde el minuto uno concentradas y sabiendo muy bien qué es lo que están buscando ellas y cómo podemos romperlo nosotras. P. ¿Y se puede pensar un poco más allá, en Estados Unidos en semifinales? R. Yo creo que en estos campeonatos hay que ir partido a partido. Ya vimos lo que pasó, tuvimos un batacazo e igual lo puede tener cualquier selección. Prefiero no hacer cábalas de qué puede pasar después, hay que hay que esperar el partido de cuartos, jugarlo y con suerte estaremos hablando, tras una victoria, de qué es lo que tenemos que hacer para sacar el partido de Estados Unidos adelante. P. Este Mundial es atípico y han preparado el último entrenamiento sin conocer a su rival. ¿Cómo se hace? R. Creo que llegados a este punto de la competición y de la preparación también para las jugadoras que llevan aquí tanto tiempo y para las que acabamos de entrar hace no tanto es más importante centrarnos en qué es lo que necesitamos hacer nosotras que en lo que el rival nos vaya a mostrar. Durante el entrenamiento sabíamos que sería una u otra selección y por lo tanto podemos tener una idea pero ya llegados a este punto creo que las jugadas que puedan hacer es menos importante a lo mejor que el pulir los detalles de las cosas que necesitamos hacer nosotras ¿Cómo vamos a defenderlas en los bloqueos? ¿Cómo vamos a estar en la pintura? Las jugadas que jugamos en ataque ¿Qué es lo que estamos buscando? ¿Qué nos ha ido bien y en qué hemos fallado? Porque ya estamos todos los equipos intentando estar muy rodados llegando al partido lo más frescas posibles entonces creo que es lo que Miguel (Méndez) ha intentado también, centrarnos en nosotras en lo que necesitamos hacer sea quien sea el rival. P. Me dice que si España es España, el miedo lo tiene que tener el rival. R. Creo que aquí estamos todos a lo mismo. Al final son unos cuartos de final creo que todos los equipos sabemos que es el partido del campeonato, es el que te mete en la lucha por las medallas o no, y por lo tanto igual que nosotras estamos pensando en los otros equipos y en lo que pueden traer o no al partido creo que el resto de equipos tienen que estar igual de preocupados por nosotras porque al final hemos demostrado que cuando estamos haciendo las cosas que queremos hacer podemos poner las cosas muy difíciles a cualquier rival y por lo tanto que se preparen ellas también. P. Este año no se ha aburrido... Europa con el Schio, WNBA con Toronto Tempo y Selección. Extenuante. R. Sí, la WNBA es una cosa distinta que no he había hecho nunca y por lo tanto están apareciendo muchas cosas nuevas o cosas que hago por primera vez. Es producto de las decisiones que tomé este año por las características de la temporada y por cómo me encontraba yo física y mentalmente y por lo tanto para lo bueno y para lo malo aquí estamos jugando al baloncesto y siguiendo para adelante. P. ¿Qué destacaría de la WNBA? ¿Cuál es la mayor diferencia con el baloncesto europeo? R. Diría que la velocidad. Se juega un baloncesto mucho más rápido y en muchas cosas mucho más simple hay mucho menos juego en 5x5 en media pista y muchas más transiciones, realmente sólo se juega en transiciones. Hay contraataques y transiciones, las jugadas son pues mucho más para romper en uno contra uno para luego partir de ahí y buscar las ventajas. Creo que es hacia donde está yendo el baloncesto en sí y Europa también irá adaptándose poco a poco a ello pero es un poco el juego como en la NBA en espacios muy abiertos y jugadoras que puedan romper mucho y el resto que sepan espaciarse bien para aprovechar esas ventajas que se generan a partir de un primer uno contra uno. P. Los chicos sólo juegan en un equipo en la NBA y luego en la selecciones. Las chicas tienen que jugar en la WNBA y luego buscarse otro equipo en Europa. ¿Se igualarán en ese aspecto las dos Ligas? La WNBA se expande y crece... R. Sí y esto va a pasar ya en estos próximos años, creo que quedan uno o dos años en los que se compaginen ambas cosas porque también son los años en los que están entrando más jugadoras europeas a probar por lo que decías que la liga se está expandiendo pero va a llegar un punto en el que la liga también se expanda tanto en número de equipos como en tiempo que se juega y por lo tanto cuando eso pase que va a ser ya la temporada que viene o la siguiente no va a permitir que se hagan las dos cosas. La gente va a tener que elegir y los clubes tendrán que adaptarse y supongo que vamos a ver un cambio en los próximos años en las competiciones internacionales y ya veremos qué cambio es y hacia qué dirección va.

articles.title: FIBA Women's World Cup 2026 Quarterfinals Qualified Teams, Schedule, Odds, Bracket Predictions
articles.summary: The stage is set for the final weekend of the 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup with the last two teams advancing to the quarterfinals on Wednesday.
articles.body:
The stage is set for the final weekend of the 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup with the last two teams advancing to the quarterfinals on Wednesday.

Australia and China claimed the final two spots, joining the United States, Spain, Hungary, France, Belgium and Germany in pursuit of a gold medal.

Here is the updated schedule for the four quarterfinal matchups and odds to win the tournament.

With the exception of a close call against Italy in which the offense could muster just 55 points, there has been nothing in Team USA's performance thus far to suggest it won't leave Berlin as champions.

Immediately after the scare against Italy, the Americans rebounded with a 41-point win over the Czech Republic.

The strongest challenger to the U.S. right now looks to be France, which had the best point differential of any team in group play at plus-127 in three games.

France and the United States are on opposite sides of the bracket, so a matchup wouldn't happen until the title game if it comes to pass. Team USA has never lost to France in six head-to-head meetings with the last matchup coming in group play at the 2020 Olympics.

This French roster is better than the group from Tokyo with Janelle Salaun and Dominique Malonga alongside Gabby Williams and Marine Johannès.

Team USA's overall depth gives it an advantage against anyone in the world, but another bad shooting night like the Italy game could open the door for France to end their quest for a fifth straight World Cup title that dates back to 2010.

articles.title: Tyler Herro's model girlfriend hits free agency after his trade to Milwaukee, court docs reveal
articles.summary: Tyler Herro and Katya Elise Henry are duking it out in court over custody and support after nearly seven years together, according to court documents.
articles.body: It seems like just yesterday that I was documenting Tyler Herro's Instagram model girlfriend Katya Elise Henry's battle through something she called "Project Booty Challenge." The reality is that it's been almost three years. A lot can and has changed in that amount of time. Back then, they had just put an apparent breakup and cheating rumors behind them. Herro was four years into his NBA career and they had a growing family. Fast-forward to June and Herro found himself in a blockbuster trade that sent Giannis Antetokounmpo from the Milwaukee Bucks to the Miami Heat. He was headed back home to Wisconsin, but would his model girlfriend be joining him? FORMER HEAT TEAMMATES BAM ADEBAYO, TYLER HERRO INVOLVED IN HEATED LAS VEGAS EXCHANGE: REPORT The answer to that question appears to have arrived on Tuesday in the form of court documents obtained by TMZ. According to the docs, Herro and Henry have called it quits and are "duking it out in court over custody and support." They've both reportedly filed lawsuits. However, the Bucks guard is said to have dismissed his case days later. He had asked the court to set up a parenting schedule and determine the amount of child support he should be paying. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE He claims to have been paying her support voluntarily since she gave birth. For her part, Henry says in her filing that she was in a relationship with Herro for almost 7 years and that she was the primary caregiver for their two children. She's asking for primary custody and wants their children to see their dad with "safeguards and parameters" in place. She reportedly cited "historical conduct" that she purposefully left out of her filing out of respect. OUTKICK IS NOW ON THE FOX APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD Things move quickly in the NBA. One minute you're a star living it up in a city like Miami and the next you're being packaged up in a deal for a bigger star and shipped off to Milwaukee. I'm not going to pretend to know why these two called it quits and if the trade played any sort of significant role in their split. I will go out on a limb and say that it didn't help.

articles.title: Caitlyn Jenner says she may enter the WNBA Draft to challenge trans athlete eligibility rules
articles.summary: Caitlyn Jenner said she told Enes Kanter Freedom she might sign up for the 2027 WNBA Draft as a "real trans person" to challenge eligibility rules.
articles.body: As Enes Kanter Freedom continues to challenge the eligibility rules of the WNBA, someone else may be tempted to do the same. Caitlyn Jenner, who Freedom has mentioned in his "peace summit" idea to talk with WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert and the WNBA task force about the eligibility controversy, mentioned on "Planet Tyrus" that she has spoken with Freedom on multiple occasions. During one of them, Jenner admitted she, as a "real trans person," told Freedom she might even consider entering the WNBA draft. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE "Enes and I have talked on the phone quite a few times, and I even told him one time — this is a couple of weeks ago — ‘Enes, I’m like a real trans person. Maybe I should sign up for the 2027 WNBA draft,’" Jenner told Tyrus. Jenner went on to mention that, back in the 1970s while becoming an American athletic icon as Bruce Jenner following a record-breaking decathlon gold medal at the 1976 Summer Olympics in Montreal, she was drafted by the then-Kansas City Kings in the NBA. These are the same Kings which now play in Sacramento following an original stint in Kansas City from 1972-85. While Jenner played basketball growing up, it was the decathlon she gave her undivided attention. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Still, the basketball skill is there, and Jenner is one of the most well-known trans persons in the country. Would the WNBA step in if the 76-year-old entered the draft? "All the WNBA had to say was, ‘You can’t play in our league because you are a man. This is a woman’s league.’ That’s it, it’s over. News cycle’s done," Tyrus said earlier in their hour-long conversation. "Maybe they don’t want the news cycle being done," Jenner responded. "Yes, that’s a good point." "Well, look at Sophie Cunningham and what happened with her — the WNBA has never got so much press." Late last month, Freedom posted a video on X following his ejection from Wintrust Arena after a spat with Chicago Sky guard Natasha Cloud in a game where they played Cunningham and the Indiana Fever. Freedom was speaking directly to Engelbert and the WNBA task force in his video, where he mentioned Jenner could moderate the "peace summit." "I’ve already spoken with her, and she’s in," Freedom wrote on X. "…Listen, the whole world is laughing at you. You have turned the #WNBA into a laughingstock. It’s time to stop hiding behind closed-door meetings, excuses, and delays and finally give the public a clear answer. Let’s have a peace summit. No shouting. No hiding. No carefully scripted statements. CAITLYN JENNER SAYS THERE'S A 'SIMPLE' SOLUTION TO END THE WNBA'S TRANS ATHLETE DEBATE "Let’s sit across the table from each other, have an open and respectful conversation, and address the questions millions of people are asking." Engelbert and the league have not responded to Freedom, whom referenced the WNBA task force that came to no decision of what justified a woman while deliberating over eligibility concerns in a recent meeting. Jenner has long been an advocate for keeping biological men out of women’s sports. She has even given her "simple" solution to end the WNBA’s trans athlete debate amid Freedom and Royce White’s endeavors. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD "They’re showing the hypocrisy of what’s going on out there in the WNBA," Jenner said of Kanter and White on "Fox News @ Night" with Trace Gallagher . "The WNBA had their meetings on this issue and Cathy (Engelbert), the head, says, ‘We talked about the trans issue but we just haven’t come up with a conclusion at this point. We will continue the conversation.’ Cathy, XX, you’re in. XY you’re out. It’s that simple. "And both these guys I think are doing a good job just to show the WNBA the hypocrisy that’s going on here. We have to protect women’s sports … I want to protect women’s sports. Title IX was one of the greatest legislations for women’s equality – that happened to be in sports."

articles.title: NBA, Nike Reveal New Warmup, Practice & Travel Gear for All 30 Teams in Photos Before 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: The NBA and Nike unveiled new warmup, practice and travel gear for all 30 teams to use during the 2026-27 season in photos posted Wednesday on X.
articles.body:
The NBA and Nike unveiled new warmup, practice and travel gear for all 30 teams to use during the 2026-27 season in photos posted Wednesday on X.

The "NBA Standard Issue Collection" primarily features oversized team logos on hoodies, pants, t-shirts and shorts.

The collection will drop in two separate launches on Sept. 15 and Oct. 12.

It reflects insights from more than 400 high school basketball players, 100 NBA players and all 30 NBA teams as well as "players and fans from around the world," per Wednesday's announcement .

Nike Basketball creative director Ross Klein explained how the collection sought to increase the connection between fans and the game.

"Basketball is more than a game — it's a culture and a form of self-expression," Klein said as part of the announcement. "This collection celebrates the attitude, creativity and individuality of today's hoopers, combining bold team identity and modern style so fans can show their connection to the game in their own way."

Products included in the collection contain bouncy fleece to bring lightweight breathability, braided drawcords, woven labels and elevated finishes.

The designs will also be incorporated in the NBA's "Specter Edition" alternate uniforms, which have yet to be revealed.

The NBA announced Wednesday that the alternates will be given to teams that have history tracing back to the "earliest chapters of the NBA" including the Sacramento Kings, Detroit Pistons, Atlanta Hawks, Golden State Warriors, New York Knicks, Philadelphia 76ers, Los Angeles Lakers and Boston Celtics.

The 2026-27 season will begin on Oct. 20.

articles.title: New York Knicks star Jalen Brunson gets the nod to host the 'Saturday Night Live' season premiere
articles.summary: Jalen Brunson will host the "Saturday Night Live" season premiere, joining Peyton Manning, LeBron James and Michael Jordan among athlete hosts.
articles.body: The first batch of hosts for the new season of "Saturday Night Live" has been announced, and New York Knicks star Jalen Brunson is about to join an elite group of athletes who have been given the nod. A group with varying degrees of success. Brunson will host the season premiere of the long-running sketch comedy series, which — believe it or not, kids — has at times in its 50-plus-year run been very funny. That will air on September 26 with musical guest Katseye. KNICKS STAR JALEN BRUNSON IS A MAN OF THE PEOPLE, REVEALS THE ONE THING HE CAN'T LIVE WITHOUT Considering he's done some stuff with WWE, I think Brunson might be one of the athletes who actually does well on SNL. As I said, over the years, we've seen some athletes who proved to be good actors and a lot who were as stiff as a board and portrayed themselves in just about every sketch. They put out an SNL sports special back in the late aughts (I downloaded it onto my iPod Touch and would watch it in study hall; that's how late aughts it was), and you'd be surprised how many solid sketches there were with athletes, even if the athlete is not a great actor in the sketch. I think the best athlete host of all time is, without question, Peyton Manning. In fact, I've even argued that his timing is so good, he probably could've been a supporting player. His high-water mark was without a doubt the United Way commercial, one of the best commercial parodies of the last 25 years. Another athlete I thought was pretty solid — and this could prove controversial — was LeBron James. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! The best sketch he was in was a bizarre Will Forte fever dream called "The Lyle Kane Show" that I can't find anywhere. So, I pulled the next best LeBron sketch, "Read to Achieve." I've quoted the line, "Don't give me this; I'm a lefty from Kansas," more times than I'd care to admit. It's so good. A standard SNL play when the athlete's acting is a little on the wooden side is to put them in a sketch where the other actor does all the work. Like this gem with Michael Jordan and Al Franken as Stuart Smalley. And one final move for athletes (not typically the host, though) is to stick them behind the "Weekend Update" desk. One of my favorites was this bit with NHL great Brett Hull. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Hopefully the SNL writers and cast — no, I can't name any of them either — have been using the summer to come up with some great material for Brunson when they reconvene at 30 Rock for the season opener at the end of the month.
